My experience at Casterton College was genuinely awful and it completely destroyed my mental health. My parents informed the school multiple times about my self-harm and the struggles I was dealing with, yet the school did absolutely nothing meaningful to support me. I felt ignored, dismissed, and treated like my wellbeing did not matter at all. Things became so bad that I eventually had to drop out because the environment was seriously affecting my mental health and making my life miserable.
The way the school handled fights and behaviour was unfair as well. Students who were simply there or unable to get away would get punished more than the people actually causing the problems. I was once trapped during a fight and physically couldn’t get out to get a teacher or leave the situation. I didn’t record anything or take part, yet I still ended up getting two terms with no social time just because I was there. On top of that, I was being shouted at by three different teachers at once. As a 14-year-old, that was honestly terrifying. I was called selfish and a liar even though I kept trying to explain that I hadn’t done anything wrong. Instead of listening, staff just made me feel blamed and humiliated.
Communication from the school was terrible. My parents constantly struggled to get in contact with anyone, and when they finally did, the main office staff were rude, dismissive, and unhelpful. Every conversation felt like we were being brushed off instead of listened to. For a school that claims to care about students, they showed very little concern or professionalism.
One of the assistant heads, Mr Raws, behaved in a way that was completely unacceptable. He would slam his fists on tables and scream at classes aggressively to the point where students were uncomfortable speaking around him. The atmosphere felt intimidating rather than educational. Even asking simple questions because you didn’t understand the work could get you shouted at, embarrassed in front of the whole class, or given behaviour points. Instead of helping students learn, some staff seemed more interested in humiliating them.
When I finally left the school, it honestly felt like they could not care less. The only thing they gave me was my art book — nothing from English, maths, or any other subject. After everything I went through, it felt like the school had completely written me off.
Overall, I would never recommend Casterton College to anyone. In my experience, the school failed badly when it came to student wellbeing, communication, and support. Instead of feeling safe or encouraged, I left feeling mentally drained, unsupported, and completely let down by the people who were supposed to help students succeed.

Their solicitor, Richard, visitied me while being detained in a Psychiatric Ward upon appealing my section. While going over my case, he pressurised me with aggressive questioning, claiming it would "prepare me for the hearing" and consequently failed to represent me properly during my CTO appeal upon discharge. He failed to read a crucial document provided by a family member written to the panel in support of my appeal, and while I attempted to respond to comments misrepresenting me, dismissed my defense as though he was acting in the interests of the panel and not myself.
After other participants finished giving evidence, he addressed me with a question. It was; why do you think you have been admitted to hospital as many times as you have? I was shocked that he was deliberately attempting to discredit me in view of the panel, and I couldn't think of an answer quickly enough. It was deeply unpleasant.
Solicitors should, according to law, always act in the best interests of the client, not just bend to norms that exist to prop up false notions of people's mental health.
I maintain that I do not suffer from any mental health issue and never have done. I refuse any psychotropic drugs and assert that I simply ended up in a cycle within a system that renders individuals dependant rather than empowered.
My assertion that I am normal unsettled Richard, and he failed to represent me when faced with members of the panel who subscribed to afforementioned long-held beliefs to do with mental health.

NEGLIGENT, DISHONEST AND UNPROFESSIONAL BEYOND BELIEF – DO NOT RISK IT

We booked a home birth with Sally through Private Midwives and the ‘care’ I received from her was so awful in so many ways that I don’t know where to begin. My baby was born by emergency caesarean due to an undiagnosed breech which was not discovered until the 2nd stage of labour.

During my labour Sally should have been performing abdominal palpitations to check the baby’s position but she did not perform a single one. So not only did Sally miss the breach – she was not even looking for it! Instead, Sally falsified these readings in the notes. Sally has since lied and said she did not perform these falsely recorded palpations because I was ‘unable to tolerate lying on my back’ for the examination – just one of the many lies told by Sally to try and shift blame onto me for her failings. Sally did not at any point during my labour ask me to lie on my back so she could perform an abdominal palpation. Towards the end of my labour, I was asked to lie on my back for a vaginal examination and did so without any difficulty. I was in no way unable to do this. This was the only vaginal examination that Sally and her colleague offered me during my labour. They did not offer me a vaginal examination until I was fully dilated had been pushing for over 2 hours. However, Sally lied in my medical notes and said that I declined numerous vaginal examinations.

Sally and her colleague also ORDERED A MCDONALD’S TAKEAWAY TO OUR HOME DURING THE SECOND STAGE OF OUR LABOUR, without our permission. They knew I was feeling sick and that this was a major fear I had about birth, and they knew that I am vegan - but they ordered it anyway, at 10:30 in the morning.

The McDonald’s takeaway arrived during an obstetric emergency, just moments after the breech had been discovered. Sally recommended I transfer to hospital for an emergency caesarean and told me and my husband to go upstairs and decide what we wanted to do. This was despite the fact I had been downstairs for my entire labour. An emergency caesarean was my worst nightmare as I have a severe needle phobia, something which was discussed at length antenatally with both Sally and her colleague. Despite this, neither Sally or her colleague offered a single word of reassurance at this point. Neither Sally or her colleague gave us any information to enable us to make an informed decision. Me and my husband were then left upstairs scared and alone for 45 minutes whilst Sally and her colleague ate McDonald’s downstairs. They have since lied and said they came upstairs but did not want to disturb me as I was very upset. Not true – we left the bathroom door wide open. We did not want to be alone.

Despite neither Sally or her colleague caring for me during this time, there was a 17-MINUTE DELAY IN RINGING THE AMBULANCE. Sally later tried to blame this on us, by saying that we ‘declined an ambulance’– another lie.

The baby’s heartrate was not monitored properly in my labour. During the 2nd stage it should have been listened to at least once every 5 minutes (as per NICE guidelines). They listened in on average just once every 29 minutes during my confirmed second stage. So, they should have been monitoring the heartrate 6 times as often as they were.

Even once the breech was discovered and they were dealing with an obstetric emergency, they did not monitor me or the baby properly. Instead they left us completely unattended whilst they ate McDonald’s takeaway. My heartrate was also not monitored properly during labour. They did not check my blood pressure even once. They did not check my temperature even once. Instead, they falsified all of these readings in the notes. These are just some of the issues and some of the lies Sally has told since the birth. There are so many more that it would be impossible to fit them all into the space available for this review. We have reported Sally to the Nursing and Midwifery Council, who are currently investigating her fitness to practice as a midwife.

The auditor appeared to have very little understanding of the subject matter and seemed to be strictly following a checklist without any real knowledge of what he was assessing. Based on our experience, we would recommend considering alternative storage providers and ensuring you obtain a full written understanding of all terms, conditions, and operational restrictions before committing.

I never write reviews, but my phone call to Shurgard Self Storage Peterborough was so offensively bad that I feel obligated to warn everyone else.

I called with a simple, honest question: I needed help figuring out the right unit size for my belongings. Not a complicated request for a self storage company, right? Wrong.

A woman named Sam picked up. From the first syllable, she made it crystal clear that my call was ruining her day. The sighs. The clipped, one-word answers. The utter refusal to engage in even the most basic back-and-forth to determine what I actually needed. When I tried to describe the volume of items, she literally said, "I don't know, just look online," as if the entire purpose of her job wasn't to, you know, help people store things.

Sam wasn't just unhelpful. She was hostile. Rude. Lazy. The kind of person who gives the entire self storage industry a bad name. I felt like an intruder for daring to ask a question about a service they supposedly offer.

So I did exactly what you should do: I hung up, drove to a competing self storage facility five minutes away, and signed a contract within ten minutes. Why? Because the person there smiled, asked questions, listened, and walked me through three different unit options like a professional human being. Imagine that.

Sam, if you hate your job that much, hand in your headset. And Shurgard management – if you're going to put someone like Sam on the front lines of customer service, you might as well hang a sign on the door that says "We don't want your business."

Customer service goes a very, very long way. In Sam's case, it went zero inches. I'm now a happy customer of your competition. Thanks for nothing.

Thank you for your response. However, attempting to attribute the issue to “timescales” or solicitors avoids the central concern raised in my review.
For the full context: from the first viewing I made it clear to the agent, vendors and solicitors that my intention was to complete before the end of the year, and this was the only reason I accepted the asking price without negotiation despite the lease nearing 80 years. The property was marketed as “no chain”, and this timeframe was known and discussed for months in advance, on multiple occasions including second viewing in the end of November.
No circumstances justify intimidating communication by your manager or suggesting that a client’s actions may negatively affect how they are viewed in “future transactions” — wording for which your agency already issued a formal apology.
As I believe this conduct fell below expected professional standards, the matter has now been formally escalated to The Property Ombudsman (TPO). I hope this leads to improved communication standards and training.

Unfortunately, my experience with this agency during a property purchase was highly disappointing. It started off well at the viewing - Aarden was highly professional, with good knowledge about the property. Unfortunately later on during the process the communication from the sales manager Josh — particularly during negotiations — crossed the line from professional guidance into unnecessary pressure and intimidation.
At one stage, I was told that my actions could affect how the agency and vendors viewed me in “future transactions,” which I found completely inappropriate and unprofessional. Following a formal complaint, the agency acknowledged that the wording used could reasonably be interpreted as intimidating and issued an apology.
I appreciate that the director responded professionally once the complaint was raised, but buyers should not have to escalate matters formally in order to be treated fairly and respectfully.
I would strongly encourage future buyers to keep all communication in writing and approach negotiations cautiously.

Title: A "Shared-Cost" Trap: My $8,000 Lesson in Professional Negligence
​I came to Olympia Publishers with three manuscripts and a heart full of trust. Fourteen months and nearly $8,000 AUD later, I am left with butchered layouts, "junk-drawer" quality illustrations, and a profound sense of professional betrayal.
​If you are an author considering their "shared-cost" model, please look at my experience before you sign:
​The "Dissection" of Art: For my photography book, Loved, Lived, Lost, Learned, I provided a professionally formatted landscape layout. They ignored it entirely, "dissecting" my work and slapping it back together with zero regard for the visual narrative. It was a hatchet job.
​The "Halloween" Illustrations: For my children’s book, Flip ‘N’ Fantastic, I provided a detailed illustration map. This was ignored. The art I received was terrifying and unnerving—completely unsuitable for children. When I complained, I was told the illustrator "chooses what to illustrate themselves." Then, they had the audacity to try and charge me an additional £4,200 for a new project to "fix" the standards they failed to meet.
​The "Wall of Silence": Staff turnover is a constant excuse. My coordinator, Kristina, vanished without a word. My emails fell into a void for weeks. When "Amy" finally appeared, she claimed she hadn't seen my emails and that the company "doesn't send updates unless there is one"—a convenient excuse for months of zero progress.
​Editorial Malpractice: In my memoir, Silent Screams, the "proofreading" was so poor that my own name was repeated five times in a single sentence. Basic POV errors (using "I" instead of "Isabella") were ignored. When I pointed this out, they attempted to charge me an additional £150 to fix the mistakes they made.
​The "Vanity" Reality: Despite promises from the Commissioning Editor that the work would not be released unless it "made sense," the production department is a factory of negligence. They treat authors like bank accounts, not creators.
​I am a pensioner living with a chronic illness (CRPS). I bet on myself by investing my savings into these stories. Olympia Publishers did not just breach their contract; they caused me significant emotional and financial harm.
​I have filed a formal complaint with Writer Beware and am seeking legal counsel for a full refund.
​My trust was bigger than their truth. Do not make the same mistake. Save your money, save your stories, and forget about Olympia Publishers.

I contacted the warranty, and I was told to go to a VAT-registered garage. I went personally to 5 garages and asked, and I also called 3 local garages, but none of them wanted to do diagnostics on Iveco. I asked if I could go to the dealership and then to a local garage for quotes, but I was told that all repairs must be done at the same garage.

In conclusion, I found that the vehicles are made only for sale, and if problems appear afterward, they don’t care. The warranty offered is almost useless, because most garages refuse to work with it, and those that do cannot perform diagnostics on Iveco.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience.

If you are being assessed for CCI GET A SECOND OPINION.

My Medserena report said that my scans showed no evidence of CCI, which was a surprise as I had very severe symptoms.

I sent my images to a Neurosurgeon in Spain who specialises in CCI and they told me that my scans are consistent with CCI and AAI and that I have brainstem compression. They showed me on my scans how they'd come to this conclusion and its glaringly obvious when its pointed out. They also said (in passing) that the Medserena scans were of poor quality.
The lady that did my Medserena scans was nice, but seemed quite stressed. She didnt tell me to lean my head on the back of the seat so I was holding my head tilted back totally unsupported and it was too painful I had to press the emergency button, so those images were wasted which was heartbreakingas it was so painful. I had to grab my head with my hands and pull it to upright again as I'd lost all strength.
They didn't tell me until after my scan that the results can take up to 10 days. They didn't send the scans to me, only to my GP, even though I'd self referred. Then after asking for the scans after 10 days they just sent me the report, I had to ask again to finally have access to my images.

All the other staff were lovely, the place was clean and seemed professional. The service they provide is essential as I dont know of anywhere else in the UK that does this kind of scan, but I definitely recommend a second opinion for CCI, which is a shame after you've spent all that money.

I purchased the Permanent Eyebrow treatment for my mum as a gift. I was confident after looking at the website and the write up about Bethan’s experience. Initially my mother was happy as the shape was good and during the initial part of the healing process you are unable to see the final results. However after time the pigment looked blocky and uneven.

The technician said she would “rectify this,” either with a ‘top up’ or she would laser remove them, but later expected us to pay extra for the correction.

Due to being unsure of what to do we sought opinions from other qualified technicians, we were told the issue appears to be caused by incorrect depth and hand pressure, especially at the tail where the skin is thinner, as well as unsuitable pigment choice for mature skin. They also confirmed that a standard top‑up would not fix the problem — the tails are already over‑saturated, and adding more pigment would only make them darker, denser, and more blotchy.

Overall, we are disappointed with both the result and how the situation was handled.

I have added photos so you can make your own informed decision.

strongly advise all potential customers to avoid this garage entirely.
I paid £6,000 for an engine replacement. Since the work was carried out, the vehicle has suffered repeated failures and has been returned to the garage on three separate occasions for the same unresolved issue. On each occasion, the fault was not properly diagnosed or repaired.
Most concerning is that the garage retained my vehicle for approximately nine months, during which time I was given repeated and inconsistent explanations for delays. Upon eventual return of the vehicle, the engine failed again on the very first day of use. This demonstrates a clear lack of reasonable care, skill, and technical competence, and strongly suggests that the work carried out falls significantly below acceptable industry standards.
There are also serious concerns regarding the MOT issued in connection with this vehicle. The vehicle—used off-road only and already subject to a DPF delete prior to their involvement (for which I hold evidence)—was passed through an MOT arranged via a garage associated with them. This is highly questionable, as at the time of testing the vehicle had:
No DPF fitted
A dangerously bulging tyre
A non-functioning indicator
Any one of these issues should have resulted in an immediate MOT failure. The fact that a certificate was issued regardless raises serious questions about the legitimacy and legality of the test.
As a result of the above, I have paid a substantial sum for work that has repeatedly failed, been deprived of my vehicle for an excessive period, and have been left with a vehicle that remains unfit for purpose.
Unless this matter is resolved with a full refund of the £6,000, I will have no hesitation in escalating the issue formally. This will include reporting the MOT irregularities to the DVSA and pursuing a complaint with Trading Standards in relation to substandard workmanship and breaches of consumer protection legislation. I will also consider initiating legal proceedings to recover my financial losses.
I would not trust this garage with any vehicle under any circumstances.

one_star_reviews.text: MCS cancelled 2 appointments with us for a boiler service. We paid upfront. Waisted a days holiday from work as 1st appointment was cancelled at short notice.

I contacted this company to repair my Samsung air source heat pump. Initially, they attended within two days, and I paid a £120 call-out fee based on their confidence that they could fix the issue.

The engineer diagnosed a faulty fan motor and blade and said I’d have a quote and the work completed “early the following week”.

From that point on, the experience went downhill.

I had to chase them repeatedly over the following week just to get a quote. Each time I called, I was fobbed off with the same excuse that they were “waiting on a supplier for pricing”. This simply didn’t add up — they had already identified the parts, and I was able to find and price them myself from the very supplier they mentioned.

The quote eventually came through 8 days later. I accepted it immediately, only to then be told it would be at least another two weeks before they could carry out the repair.

I think it’s a joke that a company can charge a £120 call-out fee, give the impression they can resolve the issue quickly, and then expect you to wait a further 2–3 weeks without heating or hot water.

At this point, we had already been without heating and hot water for a prolonged period, with two young children at home, so this level of delay and lack of urgency was unacceptable.

I then contacted another company, who ordered the parts on next-day delivery and completed the repair the following day — which just shows how unnecessary the delays had been.

Overall, I felt completely misled and repeatedly fobbed off. The initial confidence quickly turned into poor communication, excuses, and unacceptable delays. I would not recommend this company.

one_star_reviews.text:
A masterclass in how to take a pretty setting, spend money on a rebuild, charge ambitious prices, and still deliver an absolutely dreadful experience.

We booked and specifically asked to sit in the garden. Instead, we were put in what can only be described as a glass hot box on the hottest spring day recorded, while the garden we had requested sat there near empty apparently beyond the operational imagination of the staff.

The table was filthy. Not a little dusty, not “pub rustic”, but actually dirty — crumbs and food debris trapped between the slats, clearly not cleaned properly between customers. It is basic hospitality: clean the table before you put people at it.

Service was equally poor. It wasn’t busy, yet it took an age for anyone to take the order. Once the food arrived, nobody came back to ask whether everything was OK, which was probably wise, because the honest answer would have required a chair, a drink and a long debrief.

The food was a joke, and not a cheap one. The chips were cold, cost £9.50, and the portion was laughable. I’ve included a photo with an olive on top for scale, which sadly says more about the value here than any menu description ever could.

The bread was stale and had very obviously been cut hours earlier. It had that dry, unpleasant texture where it almost feels toasted, but without any colour, warmth, crispness or intention.
Just stale bread pretending to be rustic.
The rest of the food was tired, ungenerous and badly judged. A depressing little parade of things that should have been simple, but somehow weren’t.

I am not someone who expects fine dining from a pub. I have eaten at McDonald’s and I have eaten in some of the best restaurants in the country — including once spending over £1,600 on a meal for two. I can enjoy both, as long as they know what they are trying to be. This place appears to be aiming for premium pricing while delivering the energy of a motorway service station having an off day.

A large amount of the food was left, which is rare for us and says everything. Nobody noticed. Nobody asked. Nobody seemed remotely interested.

On a brighter note the onion rings were ok and the duck terrine, although served too cold, was fairly decent.

Apparently the pub burned down in 2022. Looking at what has risen from the ashes, I’m not convinced the phoenix was worth the effort. On this showing, it might genuinely have been better left as a memory — or turned into flats.

Grossly overpriced, badly served, poorly cleaned and massively overhyped. I would not return, and I certainly would not recommend it.

My experience with Wings Škoda Peterborough was extremely poor.

The first red flag came at my first service on a one-year-old car, where I was left waiting for around 6 hours without anyone properly acknowledging me.

Later, a dash cam installation under Order 58200 led to oily hand marks being left inside my car and DAB reception issues afterwards. The vehicle then had to go back for the work to be redone and the interior cleaned. I was not offered a courtesy car and was left without my vehicle for over a week.

When the car was returned to me, it was scraped on my own drive while reversing. While that damage was later repaired, it remains part of the overall experience.

The most serious issue only became apparent much later, when the dash cam was professionally removed in 2026. At that point, I was informed that the rear interior trim above the rear window had been left misaligned and appeared to have been fixed through, leaving visible screw damage.

This was not something obvious to me as a layperson at the time of the original installation, which is why it could not have been raised in 2022.

I raised this later-discovered issue in 2026, provided photographs, and escalated the matter through Škoda UK. Wings Škoda Peterborough declined to remedy the issue, taking the position that modifying the trim was part of the installation process.

I did not consent to my vehicle being altered in that way, and I do not accept that visible misalignment and exposed fixing damage represent an acceptable standard of workmanship from a main dealer.

I was also disappointed to see the later-discovered 2026 trim issue publicly characterised as though this were simply an old resolved matter from 2022, when that specific concern only came to light much later and was then raised by me through the proper channels.

Looking at the dealership’s public responses to other reviews, my personal impression is that they tend to explain or defend events rather than clearly acknowledge fault where customers have raised concerns.

Based on my own experience, the high overall rating does not reflect the standard of service I personally received.

I would be very cautious about trusting this dealership with fitting work or with resolving issues when something goes wrong.

one_star_reviews.text:
We commissioned Pestology for an expensive CCTV drainage survey (£350) to identify exactly how rats were entering our property. Their website claims an evidence-led approach that pinpoints entry routes, but in reality, the service was unprofessional, contradictory, and completely failed to deliver what was promised.

Specific failings include:
CCTV images were blurry, unclear, and often unidentifiable, with no video footage provided, making it impossible to verify any conclusions.

One image in our report was of a drain at another address which is ridiculous!

The surveyor concluded that a displaced joint was the likely rat entry point, yet the owner later stated this was unlikely and that it was due to a "possible" redundant pipe. This was not mentioned on the day of the survey and this was speculation with no evidence.

Numerous basic factual inaccuracies: electric and gas boxes mislabelled as external, references to manholes not on the map. Drainage map was incorrect and no exact identification of where the the new manhole should be. Any drainage company who carry out CCTV reports would provide this. The report should be understood by any drainage company and I have had many companies shocked with the quality of this report along with the price.

Several areas were marked as inspected but were not checked, including burrow points, extension gaps, and patio edges. Felt like pictures of the property were being taken for the sake of it but no real external inspection as promised.

They offered a second survey of which I thought my concerns would at least be communicated and basic checks finally done. However, the second surveyor was rude, unprofessional, and unaware it was a follow-up survey, leaving a pipe uncapped behind the toilet, creating a hygiene risk and another entry point. No external checks were made and we were not provided with a new report that was corrected. Instead we were given pages and pages of more blurry images and told no conclusion could be made until manhole was installed. Of which this work was quoted at approx £3500. No accountability was taken by the owner, instead assumptions were made as to why we took the survey (apparently to get money back from the seller).

Overall failures:
After two surveys, we still do not know for certain how rats are entering the property.
The CCTV surveys did not add any useful information beyond what we already knew from a prior Thames Water inspection.
The recommended “manhole” was completely unnecessary to tell us what we already knew — we had communicated the lack of a manhole at the start.
Despite claiming an evidence-led, forensic approach, they could not provide clear evidence, proper analysis, or actionable findings, and instead pushed for expensive remedial works which we already knew needed to be done.
In short, this was an expensive, misleading, and unprofessional service that failed to provide the basic purpose of a CCTV survey: clear, reliable, and evidenced findings. Pestology’s claims about pinpointing entry routes and delivering evidence-led recommendations are utterly misleading. We would not recommend them for any drainage or pest inspections. You are better off using a drainage company for the CCTV report. If they can't provide what they promised with the report or take any accountability for the poor quality, inaccuracies and contradictions, then they cannot expect customers to spend such a large sum of money trusting that they will do any job well. We were happy to part with the £3500 if they did their job well but unfortunately accuracy, quality and care does not seem to be important to pestology. We are just one of the 30 visits they do a day.

I am quite disappointed with the service I received from Ben’s Gutters.

When booking the appointment, I was informed that it would take between 30 - 60 minutes, and would feature my gutters being washed through (internally) and would cost £87. However:

1) The guy turned up at my front door 20 minutes earlier than the earliest agreed time. (Check their reviews - a lot of people have the same complaint).

2) The appointment took 17 minutes only - not 30 to 60 minutes. He arrived at 09:08, and left at 09:25. I have verified this on my CCTV. (Check their reviews - me, Tim, Matthew, Jemma, Phoebe, Paul, Dominic, Angel, Edward, Sam, Danita, Zara, Claudia, Ioanna, Steven, Andrew and Rachel have all made the same complaint.)

3) He climbed a ladder, lifted some leaves out of the gutter, put them into a bucket and left. That’s all. I’d assumed that they had some special cleaning equipment - but no. Literally just a guy and a bucket.

4) I was told that he would wash the gutters through with water. This didn’t happen. The photos of the job (which I had to contact Ben’s Gutters to obtain) show dirty gutters.

5) I was told that he should disassemble the downpipes to check/clean them. This also didn’t happen. How did they know that they weren’t blocked unless they checked?

I contacted Ben’s Gutters, who offered to reduce the bill to £60. Given the early arrival, quick finish, lack of cleaning, lack of taking the gutters apart, and the fact that it was literally a guy with a bucket, I felt that this wasn’t a suitable discount.

Ben’s Gutters offered to send someone back to rinse the gutters through. However, this doesn’t address my complaints.

HOWEVER - a further issue that I noticed, was that Ben’s Gutters record all incoming calls - without telling the caller. This is not legal. Ben’s Gutters should either have an automated message informing people of this, or have their staff inform callers. Neither of these happened. I have emailed Ben’s Gutters about this, citing specific elements of GDPR, and have been told that they will ‘update’ me. As of yet, I have not received this update. I will update this review when I have.

So - all in all - it would have been cheaper, better and more legal for me to offer someone in a local Facebook group £40 or so to lift the leaves out of the gutter into a bucket. I’ll likely do that next time. Ben’s Gutter's, for the service they supply, is over priced, over sold and poor quality.

I repeatedly had to explain the same issue, was contacted at times I had specifically said I was unavailable, and spent hours on their chat system only to be cut off and forced to start again. Eventually, I gave up and moved to another provider just to get a stable connection. Even then, the problems didn’t stop. Closing the account became another ordeal, with repeated warnings about charges and a convoluted process for returning equipment.

I returned the router in good faith using a tracked courier, only to have it rejected because their own address couldn’t accept deliveries — something entirely outside my control. If you value your time, your sanity, and a reliable internet connection, I would strongly recommend choosing a different provider.

I have spent more than an hour writing about (in probably too much detail) of the chain of events that has led me to leave a 2-star review.  But ultimately it's just too stressful, and I know Tim will pop up with a scathing reply (as he does love to have the final word 😉).

The short version is this:

I spent over £40,000 on new windows, a large sliding door, a Spitfire front door and a new back door.

Most of it is fine, and the communication was good before, during and after installation.  However, I'm left feeling that if I were to do it all over again, I'd definitely choose someone else.

These are my three gripes with what's been delivered and fitted.  I've spoken to Tim about these issues several times, but he doesn't see any of these issues as his problem.  It's not good enough in my opinion.

1. I have a bay window that has a lovely new aluminium window in it, but also retains some uPVC trim from the old window that's over 20 years old.  Why Aluhome chose to leave this I don't know.  I do know that they refuse to remedy it.

one_star_reviews.text:
My lovely dad spent one week in this awful place and the effects of his stay were heartbreaking. In October 2024, having been the recipient of care in his own home for several months, my mum and I were at breaking point. We asked for a weeks respite to visit a friend for a few days, it is a decision that will haunt me forever.

Dad was unwell and generally quite infirm, but the week before he stayed here he was able to walk on the spot and feed himself. He was clean, his pressure sores were responding to treatment and his appetite was good. I visited him the day after he was admitted and the night before he was due to come home.

That night he was sat bolt upright in bed with his feet pressed against the bed footer, corresponding to the worst of his pressure sores. He was cold, his room was cold, he had nothing but a thin blanket to cover him. He told me he didn’t feel “too well.” He asked me if I could cover him with his coat. On his return to us the following day he rapidly deteriorated. I rang the helpline who called an ambulance, the paramedics noted ‘clear evidence of neglect.’

He was raw where he had been wiped abrasively, he had open sores and ingrown hairs all around his lower regions. His catheter bag had been shoved inside his trousers for the return journey, although nobody had thought to tell me. He wasn’t clean. He was so weak he could no longer hold a cup. But most of all his pressure sores had severely worsened. The overall effect was a sea change.

My mum sobbed when she saw the state dad was in, months of intensive, gentle, humane care on her part had been completely undone in a week. Clearly dad had been left in bed for the duration without any kind of proper care, let alone stimulation. He told me the food was awful and that the staff “don’t know what they’re doing.”

A fantastically interesting and intelligent man with a great sense of humour, I asked the staff to please look after him. I cried when I was told he was in safe hands. When I came to collect him, the same person who told me he would be well cared for commented that he did have a good sense of humour. “I don’t know how they would have as ascertained that,” my dad told me. Clearly, they took him for a fool as well as just another inmate not worth the time.

A week after his discharge from Holmleigh, dad was admitted to St Barnabas, four weeks later he died. I would seriously caution anyone against using this nursing home. For my dad I feel it constituted the beginning of the end and for this I will never forgive them or myself.

We visited Tsuki Japanese Restaurant within the last week and, sadly, we won’t be returning.

The concept has potential, but right now the experience feels hard work rather than enjoyable.

When we arrived, the restaurant was around half empty and lacked any real atmosphere. As a group of six (five adults and one child), we headed to the bar for a drink, but were asked by a waitress to return to the entrance foyer to be seated properly. This felt odd given how quiet the restaurant was.

We were also told the extractor system in the kitchen was broken, which meant the front door had to be propped open. Unfortunately, we were seated right next to it and spent the entire meal freezing, to the point where we kept our coats on. We raised this a few times, but the only solution offered was a small fan, which made little difference, it genuinely felt like sitting outside.

We opted for the buffet at £39 per head (rising to £45 at weekends, which felt unusual), and were given an iPad to order all food and drinks. The system was clunky and confusing, especially for some of our group. One person hadn’t brought their glasses, and another was 70, so passing one device around made it slow and frustrating, taking several minutes per person just to place an order.

It would have been far better for a member of staff to take the first round of orders and bring something simple like miso soup while we got settled. Instead, we were left trying to navigate the system in a cold restaurant, which took away from the whole experience.

Food took around 45 minutes to arrive and, when it did, it was just OK, not bad, but certainly not worth the price given everything else , also no child option on the food, and you had to pay extra for deserts!

Overall, it’s a shame, because with a few improvements, particularly around service, ordering, and basic comfort, it could be a really good place. But as it stands, the experience just isn’t there, and unfortunately we wouldn’t return or recommend it.

My own meal—a beetroot wellington—was supposed to come with tater tots and seasonal greens, but instead arrived with chips and peas. By that point, we had already waited so long that we didn’t feel it was worth raising another issue.

The response from Volvo Cars UK is that they cannot help with my complaint. Absolute unbelievable. The only way to get a warranty repair is to pay for it yourself. Kerbside Motors

Just an update on the water leak, I got into the car today Sunday 18 January 2026 only to see the " Low coolant level turn off engine" warning light on again. Topped up the coolant level again  before I could continue to drive. I suppose that the ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY OF SELF FIXING WATER HOSES IS A MYTH.

This is the Volvo Cars UK Ltd Statement.
We design cars that put people first – and that’s what makes a Volvo car different. We push technological boundaries to find new ways of advancing safety, adding more enjoyment to the car experience and making daily life easier.

I think the following is more appropriate.
We design cars that come with a warranty that is solely at our discretion. We push the boundaries to increase our profit margins daily.

I own a Volvo XC60 2023 registration so its still under warranty. Last Friday morning I started the car as normal, a few seconds later a warning displayed low coolant level stop the car. I stopped the engine and looked into the coolant reservoir and noticed that there was no coolant visible. I drove the car to work and got one our technicians to put it on the car ramp to see if he could see a leak.
There was a formed coolant hose ( OEM part only I would imagine) running from the front underneath to the rear of engine. It was tight to the front engine housing and it appeared to have rubbed on the housing and worn through so it was leaking. Not a major leak however it is one of the lowest parts of the cooling system so it will leak even when the engine is stopped. Meaning it is possible the cooling system could be drained.

As it is rubbing on the engine cover I surmise it was fitted incorrectly or it is a design fault. As the car is still under warranty I contacted Riverside Volvo Hull and explained the situation. The car was booked into their service department for a replacement hose to be fitted on Tuesday 13 January. Riverside service department are familiar with this fault and it is not the first XC60 to visit their workshop to get this warranty job completed.

The car went into Riverside Hull for the repair but they didn’t carry out the repair. Instead they brought the car out of the workshop and gave it back to my partner and said they couldn’t repair the car as it had stopped leaking. Volvo Cars would not honour the warranty as the leak had crystallised and it was not leaking when they looked at it. Apparently Riverside Volvo have to take a video of the leak before Volvo will honour the warranty and as it wasn’t leaking so they couldn’t fix it. Several telephone conversations between myself and Riverside before I explained to my Partner she had wasted a half a day, Riverside would not be repairing the car, so it was time to come home. I find the whole experience bizarre and unprofessional, I was not contacted by Riverside when the car was in the workshop to explain the situation nor was I given an estimate to get the repair carried out at my cost.

So now I have a car with a faulty leaking formed hose, the integrity of the hose has been compromised. It is still rubbing on the engine so what comes next, will it burst and leave the car inoperable at the side of the road. Will it drain the coolant overnight and leave the car inoperable. I now have 5 litres of coolant in the car to top it up when need be. I am not sure that will be enough in an emergency, such uncertainty instead of piece of mind. I wonder during assembly or manufacturing has this fault been modified.

I do understand the position Riverside Volvo Hull are in as they are governed by Volvo’s interpretation of their warranty claims and terms. Communication throughout was frustrating. Questions were often only partially answered, requiring repeated follow-ups and causing unnecessary delays. For something as significant as a mortgage, I would expect clear, complete and confident guidance—not vague or selective responses.

There was also a lack of proper exploration of viable options. Alternative lenders and approaches were not meaningfully considered, and assumptions were made about what documentation could or could not be obtained, which later proved incorrect.

Most concerningly, after indicating we were ready to proceed, the adviser withdrew from acting due to workload rather than arranging for the case to be reassigned. This left us in a difficult position and caused avoidable delays during an already stressful process.

CMA Action and Reforms (2025-2026)
Prescription Fee Cap: Vets are now ordered to cap written prescription fees at £21 for the first medicine and £12.50 for additional drugs.

Transparency Mandate: Vets must inform pet owners that medicine may be cheaper online and provide the option for a prescription.
Practice Ownership: Vets must disclose if they are part of a larger corporate group.

Steps for Pet Owners
Request Prescriptions: You can ask for a prescription and fill it at a lower-cost online pharmacy.

Request Estimates: Always ask for a written, itemised estimate for treatment plans.

Shop Around: Prices vary significantly between practices, so compare costs.

Complain: If unhappy, check the vet’s complaints procedure and use the free Veterinary Client Mediation Service.

I purchased three bras from this shop. One of them developed a hole after being worn once and washed once, making it unusable.

I travelled 45 minutes to return the item after being told “we can sort something out,” only to then be told in the shop  that because I had washed it at 30 degrees, I had not followed the care label and therefore would not receive a refund.

The owner inspected the item and took photographs of the fault, so the damage was clearly acknowledged. However, I was refused a refund on the basis that the manufacturer would not reimburse them, which is disappointing as responsibility lies with the retailer under the Consumer Rights Act 2015.

I was also told I would receive the items back, but I am still waiting for them to be returned and have had no further response.

It should also be made clear at the point of sale that these bras are hand wash only. This was not highlighted and is not particularly practical for a sports bra, which you would reasonably expect to be able to wash easily after use.

I found that the staff were very friendly and helpful when I was purchasing, but the experience felt very different when there was an issue to resolve. I can see from previous reviews that I am not the only person to highlight this as an issue .

Overall, this has been a very frustrating experience. I would not expect items at this price point to fail after one wash, and the lack of resolution and communication has been very disappointing.

⭐ 1 Star – Poor Customer Service & Questionable Product Condition
Dreadful first experience with Oliver’s BabyCare.
I ordered two car seats (one for each vehicle). Delivery was prompt, however one of the boxes had clearly been previously opened and re-taped. Upon opening, it was evident the item had either been returned or previously handled — the internal packaging was not intact, the anchor straps were fully unravelled, and protective foam was incorrectly placed rather than secured.
The second seat appeared new, however when installed using ISOFIX and tested with our 2-year-old, the impact shield was extremely tight — even on its maximum setting. We struggled to secure it properly, and it caused visible discomfort to our child.
For context, the product is advertised as suitable for use with the impact shield up to approximately 4 years (21kg / 105cm). Our son is 2 years old and well within these limits, yet the seat is already impractically tight.
I contacted Oliver’s BabyCare requesting a collection and refund on the basis that:
One item was not supplied in new condition
The product is not suitable for its intended use
Unfortunately, this is where the experience deteriorated. The response has been dismissive and unhelpful, with the company attempting to treat this as a standard return and expecting me to cover return costs and transport two large boxes myself.
I have advised the items are available for collection. If this is not arranged, I will proceed with a chargeback / Section 75 claim via my credit card provider.
A company is judged by how it handles problems — not when everything goes smoothly. Based on this experience, customer service falls well below expectations.

UPDATE (following business response):

I note the response from Oliver’s BabyCare, however I do not agree with their characterisation of this as a “change of mind” return.

My concerns have been consistent throughout:
1) One of the items was not presented as new, with clear signs of having been opened and incorrectly repackaged
2) The product is not fit for purpose in practice, despite my child being well within the stated specifications

I would also highlight a contradiction in the response. It is stated that items are “thoroughly inspected prior to dispatch” and not previously opened, however one of the boxes was clearly re-taped and internally disturbed, whilst the other arrived factory sealed. This inconsistency raises further questions regarding handling prior to dispatch.

This is not a subjective preference issue. The impact shield is so tight that it has to be forced into place and causes visible distress to my child, which raises genuine concerns around safe and practical use.

Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, goods must be:
- Of satisfactory quality
- As described
- Fit for purpose

In this case, I do not believe those requirements have been met.

I have made the items available for collection and simply requested a reasonable resolution. Despite this, the company continues to rely on its returns policy rather than addressing its obligations under consumer law.

I will now be proceeding with a chargeback / Section 75 claim.

I will update this review further depending on how the matter is resolved. As the public can see yous are dismissive and have a total disregard for consumer law..

NEGLIGENT, DISHONEST AND UNPROFESSIONAL BEYOND BELIEF – DO NOT RISK IT

We booked a home birth with Amie through Private Midwives and the ‘care’ I received from her was so awful in so many ways that I don’t know where to begin. My baby was born by emergency caesarean due to an undiagnosed breech which was not discovered until the 2nd stage of labour.

Amie failed to suspect the breech during 3 antenatal appointments, where she recorded the baby as head down. I should have been sent for a scan to check the presentation, but I wasn’t. But what is much worse, and what we only learnt later, is that Amie and her colleague should have been performing abdominal palpations during my labour to check the position of the baby. They did not do this even once. So not only did these midwives miss that the baby was breech – they were not even looking! Instead, they falsified these readings in the notes.

AMIE ALSO DISAPPEARED FROM MY HOMEBIRTH FOR 3 HOURS, just 1 hour after she had arrived. Not a word was said by either midwife about where she had gone or why. We later found out that AMIE HAD TAKEN HERSELF UPSTAIRS AND SLEPT IN OUR BED, WITHOUT OUR PERMISSION.

Amie and her colleague also ORDERED A MCDONALD’S TAKEAWAY TO OUR HOME DURING THE SECOND STAGE OF LABOUR. They knew I was feeling sick and that this was a major fear I had about birth, and they knew that I am vegan - but they ordered it anyway at 10:30 in the morning. They have since lied and said I gave them permission to do this. I did not.

The McDonald’s takeaway arrived during an obstetric emergency, just moments after the breech had been discovered. It was recommended I transfer to hospital for an emergency caesarean and me and my husband were told to go upstairs and decide what we wanted to do. This was despite the fact I had been downstairs for my entire labour. An emergency caesarean was my worst nightmare as I have a severe needle phobia, something which was discussed at length antenatally with Amie. Despite this, neither Amie or her colleague offered a single word of reassurance at this point. Neither Amie or her colleague gave us any information to enable us to make an informed decision. Me and my husband were then left upstairs scared and alone for 45 minutes whilst Amie and her colleague ate McDonald’s downstairs. They have since lied and said they came upstairs but did not want to disturb me as I was very upset. Not true – we left the bathroom door wide open. We did not want to be alone. They could not have come upstairs without our knowing it.

Despite neither Amie or her colleague caring for me during this time, there was a 17-MINUTE DELAY IN RINGING THE AMBULANCE. Amie and her colleague also tried to blame this on me and my husband, by saying that we told her not to ring one – another lie.

The baby’s heartrate was also not monitored properly in my labour. During the 2nd stage it should have been listened to at least once every 5 minutes (as per NICE guidelines). Amie and her colleague listened in on average just once every 29 minutes during my confirmed second stage. So, they should have been monitoring the heartrate 6 times as often as they were.

Even once the breech was discovered and they were dealing with an obstetric emergency, they did not monitor me or the baby properly. During this time, they left us completely unattended whilst they ate McDonald’s takeaway. My heartrate was also not monitored properly during labour. They did not check my blood pressure even once. They did not check my temperature even once. Instead, they falsified all of these readings. These are just some of the issues with the ‘care’ I received and some of the lies Amie has told since the birth. There are so many more that it would be impossible to fit them all into the space available for this review. We have reported Amie to the Nursing and Midwifery Council, who are currently investigating her fitness to practice as a midwife.

I do not normally leave reviews, but after the experience we have had dealing with this firm, I felt it was important to share it.

Our experience dealing with this firm in relation to the administration of an estate has been extremely poor. The estate administration has now been ongoing for approximately four years, during which time communication and transparency have been consistently lacking.

As beneficiaries named in the Will, we did not instruct this firm ourselves, but unfortunately have had to deal with them throughout the administration process. More recently, after attempting to obtain clarity regarding the status of the estate, we experienced repeated delays, unanswered emails, and direct questions being ignored.

Even when updates were eventually provided, they still failed to address many of the reasonable questions we had raised regarding the administration of the estate, which only added to the ongoing frustration and lack of clarity surrounding the matter.

On multiple occasions we were told that further updates would be issued “shortly” or within a specified timeframe, only for those deadlines to repeatedly pass without explanation or apology. Most recently, we were informed that a further update had already been prepared and was simply awaiting approval. Weeks later, nothing has still been sent and further correspondence has again gone unanswered.

What has been most frustrating is not simply the delay itself, but the complete lack of accountability and transparency throughout the process. Even after formally raising concerns and requesting details of the firm’s complaints procedure, we still received no substantive response.

We fully appreciate that estate matters can sometimes be complex. However, there is no excuse for beneficiaries to be left with so little information for such a prolonged period of time while communication remains this poor and inconsistent.

At this stage we have entirely lost confidence in the firm’s handling of the matter and would strongly encourage others to carefully consider all available options before dealing with or instructing this firm in relation to estate administration matters.
